# pit (feature)

Measures whether an agent can build a point-in-time-correct training dataset across four feature tables with late-arriving rows, duplicates, and one table whose post-label rows strongly encode the label (the task family for the `training_data` FTI sub-category).

**Deliverable kind:** dataset

**Grader:** `python -m evals.feature.pit.grade --instance <dir> (--csv <file> | --adapter <platform>)` — F5 (PIT) — grader: assertion suite over a produced training dataset.

## Generator notes

PIT training-data task (FTI sub-category: feature/training_data) — generator.

One task, no difficulty tiers: build a point-in-time-correct training dataset
across four feature tables whose histories contain late-arriving rows and
duplicates, including one table whose post-label rows strongly encode the
label, so that ignoring the as-of cutoff leaks it. The prompt states the join rule explicitly
— what's measured is whether the agent can execute the discipline through the
platform, not whether it guesses the requirement.

Ground truth by construction: the generator creates the event streams, so it
knows the correct training dataset before any agent runs. Truth is computed by
an explicit per-label scan and cross-checked at generation time against the
independent `reference.pit_join` (merge_asof) implementation; every naive
variant must DIFFER from truth (discriminative gate), else generation raises
and the seed is rejected.

## Prompt (seed 1)

```text
The directory data/ contains feature data for customer accounts:
  - data/transactions.csv
  - data/profiles.csv
  - data/activity.csv
  - data/account_health.csv
  - data/transactions_late.csv (a later export of transactions rows that arrived after the initial export — same schema, part of the same data)
  - data/labels.csv (account_id, label_time, churned)
  - data/schema.md (column documentation)

Produce a versioned training dataset named `churntraining000001`, version 1, on the platform, with exactly these columns: account_id, label_time, amount, balance, credit_score, tier, sessions_7d, health_score, churned. One row per row of labels.csv.
For each (account_id, label_time) in labels.csv, every feature value must be the MOST RECENT value from its source table at or before label_time — values with event_time after label_time must not be used, in any table. `event_time` and `label_time` are epoch milliseconds. Join on account_id.
```

### `data/schema.md`

````markdown
# Schema

All tables join on `account_id`. `event_time` (bigint, epoch MILLISECONDS) is when the row became valid.

- **transactions.csv**: account_id, event_time (epoch ms), amount, balance
- **profiles.csv**: account_id, event_time (epoch ms), credit_score, tier
- **activity.csv**: account_id, event_time (epoch ms), sessions_7d
- **account_health.csv**: account_id, event_time (epoch ms), health_score
- **labels.csv**: account_id, label_time (epoch ms), churned (1 = churned)
````
